get.summary:
Public and unauthenticated on purpose — deliberately the only endpoint in
this module without JwtAuthGuard. Both sides need the taxonomy before they
have a token: a business picks its category during onboarding, and a
customer browses categories before signing up at all.

Seeded by prisma/seed.ts.

post.summary: Replaces the location's whole week of operating hours in one call.

delete.summary:
Retires a service EVERYWHERE. Soft delete: flips isActive to false so past
appointments still resolve.

patch.summary:
Turns a service on or off at ONE branch (§74).

A PATCH, not a DELETE: the offer row and its price survive a pause. A
separate decision from retiring below — "not here, for now" rather than
"we have stopped doing this at all".

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Omit for every business, whatever its status.

delete.summary: Soft delete — sets status REMOVED, never drops the row.

parameters.name: durationMinutes
parameters.description:
Optional, defaulting to the grid unit. A caller who has not yet picked a
service still wants to see the shape of the day, and 15 minutes is the
shortest thing that can be booked — so it yields the most permissive
(largest) honest slot list rather than an arbitrary guess.

Note it is NOT constrained to a multiple of 15: start times sit on the
grid, but a 50-minute service is perfectly legal and simply ends off-grid.

patch.summary:
Changes the fee for FUTURE bookings only. Appointments already booked keep
the amounts computed at their booking time — see DECISIONS.md.

get.summary:
The manual USD -> provider-currency rate, and how stale it is.

Manual by deliberate MVP scope: there is no live FX feed, and pretending
otherwise would be worse than an admin knowing they own this number.

patch.summary:
Sets the rate used to convert deposits at charge time.

Applies to FUTURE charges only. An appointment already paid keeps the
amount and rate it was actually charged at — see the snapshot fields on
Appointment.

How old the rate may get before it is reported stale.

Reporting only. Nothing here can block a booking or a payment (§37.3).

get.summary:
How long after an appointment resolves before its money may be paid out.

The hold in force AT RESOLUTION TIME is the one that applies. Changing this
affects appointments resolved afterwards; it never rewrites a date already
set on an entry (§38.1).

How to render money, so no client has to guess (§70.1).

Every amount this API returns is an integer in the MINOR units of
`code`, and how many of those make one major unit is a property of the
currency — two for dollars, none for francs. A client that hardcodes a
division by 100 is correct in one country and wrong by a factor of a
hundred in another, which is the §55.2 mistake moved to the front end
where it is harder to see.

Served unauthenticated, like the operator list: it is a fact about the
platform, needed before anyone signs in, and it reveals nothing.

post.summary:
Starts collecting the deposit through the payment provider.

Replaced the temporary `mark-deposit-paid` seam, which moved the status
without moving money. The appointment stays PENDING_PAYMENT until the
payment is confirmed — see AppointmentsService.initiateDepositPayment.

Verification without the code (§54.3).

OWNER and MANAGER only, unlike `verify` above, which STAFF may also use.
Taking a code the customer reads out is counter work; deciding to proceed
WITHOUT one is a judgement about whether a stranger is who they say they
are, and it is recorded against whoever makes it.

get.summary:
Live payment status, queried straight from the provider.

Exists so a frontend can poll immediately after initiating rather than
waiting for the background job's cycle. Open to either participant: the
business needs to see whether the deposit landed just as much as the
customer does.

post.summary: Either the customer who booked it or an active member of its business.

Opens (or returns) the inquiry thread with a business.

CUSTOMER-only: a business does not cold-open a conversation with someone
who has not contacted them, which would make this an outbound-marketing
tool rather than a support channel.

Sends a message: text, a photo, or both.

multipart/form-data so a photo can ride along with the text, the same shape
as the gallery upload, and reusing its exact limits — 15MB, jpg/png/webp —
plus MulterExceptionFilter so an oversized file gets the same clear error
rather than a bare 500.

get.summary:
What the platform should currently be holding, by currency.

The figure to compare against the provider's actual balance. Nothing
compares it automatically; producing the number is the point.

patch.summary:
Executes a BillingAdjustment — §25.2 renamed `appliedInvoiceId` to
`settledAt` + `settlementRef` for exactly this call.

Sends ONE payout through the operator (§64.3).

One route, one payout, and no batch equivalent. A bug in a batch pays every
business wrongly before anyone notices; a bug here pays one and stops.

info.title: Booking platform API
info.description: One backend serving the Customer, Business and Admin apps (§4). Money amounts are integer MINOR UNITS of the currency named beside them.

role.description:
Which kind of account to CREATE, when this email has never signed up.

Optional, and ignored entirely for an email that already exists — that user
logs in as whoever they already are, and the body does not get a vote
(§50.1). Required only for a genuinely new email, enforced in the service
where the answer to "does this user exist?" is known.

Still restricted to BUSINESS | CUSTOMER, so ADMIN accounts remain
impossible to self-register (§3). That was always the rule; the bug was
that it also made existing admins impossible to AUTHENTICATE.

reason.description:
Required, exactly as it is for hiding a review (§28): moderation with no
recorded reason cannot be reviewed later or explained to the customer it
happened to — and the customer is told, so there has to be something to
tell them.

latitude.description:
REQUIRED on create since §43.2. A location with no coordinates cannot
appear in a distance search, and a customer looking for somewhere nearby is
the whole point of the discovery module — a business that onboards without
them is invisible to the search that matters most.

The column stays nullable: rows created before this genuinely have no
coordinates and there is nothing honest to backfill them with.

capacity.description:
Concurrent appointments this location can run.

At least 1 — a location that can serve nobody is a closed location, which
is what opening hours and schedule exceptions are for. Capped at 500 to
catch a fat-fingered entry rather than to express a real ceiling.

offers.description:
Where this service is offered, and for how much at each branch (§72).

At least one: a service offered nowhere cannot be booked by anybody, and
creating one is almost always a mistake rather than an intention. A branch
can be removed later, which is the honest way to stop offering it there.

depositPercentage.description:
Share of the price the customer pays up front to hold the slot.

The lower bound is NOT expressed here: it is the live platform fee from
PlatformSetting, which an admin can change at runtime, so validating it
needs a database read and happens in ServicesService.

providerCurrency.description:
ISO 4217 code the provider charges in. "EUR" for MTN's sandbox.

Optional so a rate can be corrected without restating the currency; when
omitted the stored currency is kept.

exchangeRateUsdToProviderCurrency.description:
How many units of providerCurrency one USD buys.

Excluded minimum, not `@Min(0)`: a rate of exactly zero would convert every
deposit to nothing and charge customers zero, which is a worse failure than
refusing the value.

exchangeRateStalenessHours.description:
How many hours old the exchange rate may be before it is reported stale.

Zero is allowed and means "always warn" — legitimate for a currency moving
fast enough that any stored rate is suspect. Capped at a month, past which
the warning has stopped being a warning about anything.

payoutHoldDays.description:
Days between an appointment resolving and its money becoming payable.

Zero is allowed and means "payable immediately" — a deliberate choice for a
platform that trusts its businesses, not an accident. Capped at 30: a hold
longer than a month stops being a settling window and starts being the
business financing the platform.

platformFeePercentage.description:
Percentage of the service price taken as the platform fee.

Two decimal places, matching the Decimal(5,2) column. Capped at 100 because
a fee above the whole price is nonsense, and every service's
depositPercentage must be at least this value — so raising it too far would
make existing services unsaveable.

startTime.description:
Requested start, as an ISO-8601 instant (e.g. "2026-09-15T07:00:00.000Z").

Only the start is accepted. endTime is derived server-side from the
service's durationMinutes — letting a client send it would let them book a
15-minute slot for a 4-hour service.

phoneNumber.description:
Payer's number in MSISDN form: digits only, country code first, no plus and
no spaces (e.g. "211920100200"). That is the shape MTN expects in
`payer.partyId`, and normalising here means the provider never has to guess
what a "+211 92 010 0200" was meant to be.

provider.description:
Which operator to collect through (§58.1).

Optional, and it WINS when supplied. The platform infers the operator from
the number's prefix, which is right most of the time and wrong for anyone
who has ported their number to another network — and a ported customer has
no other way to be paid from. So the inference is a default the caller can
always overrule, never a verdict.

reason.description:
Optional in the shape, REQUIRED when a business cancels — enforced in the
service, because only the service knows which side the caller is on.

A business cancellation costs the business money under §25, so it should be
a deliberate act with a stated reason. A customer cancelling their own
booking owes nobody an explanation.

gatewayChargeMinor.description:
What the payment gateway charged to process the refund, in MINOR UNITS OF
THE SETTLEMENT CURRENCY — the currency the provider actually charged in
(§45.4). REQUIRED when a business cancels an appointment whose deposit was
paid.

Supplied, never derived. The MoMo integration does not report its own
charge on a transaction or a refund (§36.2), so computing it from a
percentage constant would put a number in the ledger that the provider's
statement contradicts — and a ledger that cannot be reconciled is not
doing its job. Zero is allowed: sometimes there is no charge.

ticketId.description: The ticket the decision came out of, so the reclassification is auditable.

body.description:
Optional, because a photo alone is a valid message. The service rejects
the case where neither this nor a file is present — a rule the database
also enforces via the messages_content_not_empty CHECK.

Arrives as a multipart text field.

settlementRef.description:
The provider's reference for the money movement, where there is one.

Optional, unlike a payout's: some adjustments are settled by netting
against a future payout rather than by a separate transfer, and inventing a
reference for those would make a reconciliation look complete when it is
not.

body.description: The opening message. A ticket with no description is not actionable.

appointmentId.description:
Optional. When present the reporter is verified to be a party to it —
in the service, not only in a guard.

Note reporterType is NOT accepted here: it is derived from the
authenticated user's role, so a customer cannot file as a business.

isInternal.description:
Admin-only. Ignored entirely on the reporter-facing endpoint, and rejected
for non-admins on the admin endpoint, so a reporter can never author a note
they would then be unable to see.

Arrives as a multipart text field, hence the explicit transform.

resolutionNote.description: Required when moving to RESOLVED; enforced in the service.

hiddenReason.description:
Required. Hiding customer feedback without recording why is the kind of
moderation that cannot be reviewed later or explained in a dispute.

reference.description:
The provider's reference for the transfer. Required: a payout marked paid
with nothing to look it up by cannot be reconciled against a statement, and
the statement is the only thing that proves the money left.

reason.description:
Required, like every other moderation reason here. Marking a payout failed
puts its money back in the pool, and someone will ask later why it did not
go out.

verificationNote.description:
How the admin confirmed the number belongs to this business.

Required. This is the record of the only irreversible decision the platform
makes — "verified" with no account of how is not something anyone can audit
after money has gone to the wrong place.

reason.description: Required: the business has to be told what to fix.

msisdn.description:
The mobile-money number payouts are sent to, in E.164.

The SHAPE is checked here; the expected country prefix is checked in the
service, because it is configurable (§48.2).
